title: A growing country
note: Drafted for Prompt 12 (Unit 5). Every lesson is a draft until a person reviews it (content/course/README.md).

listen.explanationKey: What territory did the United States buy from France in 1803?
facts: In 1803, the United States bought the Louisiana Territory from France. It doubled the size of the country.
The United States wanted the port of New Orleans, on the Mississippi River, for trade. France needed money for its wars in Europe, so it agreed to sell.
President Thomas Jefferson paid France $15 million for the land, from the Mississippi River to the Rocky Mountains.
The United States fought several wars in the 1800s: the War of 1812, the Mexican-American War, the Civil War and the Spanish-American War.
The country kept growing. In 1867, it bought Alaska, which is now the largest state.

story.say: In 1803, the United States bought the Louisiana Territory from France.

help.simpler: The United States bought a very large area of land from France.
help.example: This was called the Louisiana Purchase.
help.why: The test asks what territory the U.S. bought from France in 1803.

story.say: The Louisiana Purchase doubled the size of the country.

help.simpler: After the purchase, the country was two times as big.
help.example: Doubled means it became two times bigger.
help.why: It shows how fast the young country grew.

story.say: The United States wanted the port of New Orleans, on the Mississippi River, for trade.

help.simpler: A port is a place where ships load and unload goods.
help.example: Farmers sent their crops down the river to New Orleans.
help.why: This is why the United States wanted the land.

check.prompt: What territory did the United States buy from France in 1803?

story.say: France needed money for its wars in Europe, so it agreed to sell.

help.simpler: France was fighting wars and needed money.
help.example: Selling the land gave France money for its army.
help.why: This is why France said yes.

story.say: President Thomas Jefferson paid France $15 million for the land.

help.simpler: Jefferson was President. He made the deal with France.
help.example: Fifteen million dollars was a very large amount of money then.
help.why: It connects to Jefferson: he doubled the size of the country.

story.say: The land went from the Mississippi River to the Rocky Mountains.

help.simpler: The land was in the middle of today’s country.
help.example: The Rocky Mountains are big mountains in the West.
help.why: It helps you picture how big the purchase was.

check.statement: France sold the Louisiana Territory because it needed money.

story.say: The United States fought several wars in the 1800s.

help.simpler: There were four big wars in the 1800s.
help.why: The test asks you to name one war of the 1800s.

story.say: They were the War of 1812, the Mexican-American War, the Civil War and the Spanish-American War.

help.simpler: These four wars were all in the 1800s.
help.example: The Civil War was fought from 1861 to 1865.
help.why: Any one of these four is a right answer on the test.

check.prompt: Tap the war that was fought from 1861 to 1865.

story.say: The country kept growing. In 1867, it bought Alaska.

help.simpler: Later, the United States bought Alaska too.
help.example: Alaska is far in the north, next to Canada.
help.why: It shows the country kept growing after 1803.

story.say: Alaska is now the largest state.

help.simpler: Of all 50 states, Alaska has the most land.
help.example: Alaska is more than twice as big as Texas.
help.why: It helps you remember how the country grew.

check.prompt: Name one war fought by the United States in the 1800s.
